novum_candidates.description: The 'hipwiggler,' a supposedly deadly nocturnal creature that eats a sleeping man from head to toe (or vice versa) and is caught by making a noise like a 'loofmad' while standing on a persimmon stump. It is entirely a fabrication invented by Magpie to prank the credulous Professor Ajax.

novelty.rationale: The hipwiggler is presented within the story itself as a tall tale invented to fool Ajax, not as a real feature of the story universe. Nothing about the empirical norm of the storyworld is actually altered; the frontier remains an ordinary, non-fantastic setting. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the implied empirical norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: No coherent, systematic, immanent account is offered; the creature's described behavior (eating from one end and back, sleeping only noon-to-one, caught by a nonsense noise) is explicitly comedic nonsense with no internal logic, and the narrative confirms it does not exist.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: While the hipwiggler recurs as a running joke, it is an incidental prank device inside a broader comic frame narrative about an educated fool. It does not determine the overriding narrative logic, which is the satire of over-education.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No estrangement evidence IDs were supplied in the prompt; the evidence set is empty, so no reader-facing contrast, storyworld consequence, or character-reaction evidence can be cited.
